Each alias either registry-misses (because the alias name is not registered as a tool) or routes to its own distinct registered handler (read_file -> read_file, search_files -> search_files). note_on_read_file_and_search_files: Two entries (read_file and search_files) are registered in the @cline/agents default bundle as DISTINCT tools, not aliases. At the configured-agent filter, they canonicalize to the sibling name (read_file -> read_files, search_files -> search_codebase). At top-level dispatch, they are dispatched exactly to their own registered handler (read_file -> read_file executor, search_files -> search_files executor). B4-child-canonical verifies that `tools: [bash, read_file]` canonicalizes to `[run_commands, read_files]` in the CHILD runtime's toolset — i.e. the configured-agent filter does NOT preserve the alias naming.
